items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to requiring certain state
owned and operated parking garages, open parking lots and other parking
facilities to install and maintain charging stations for plug-in electric
vehicles
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1535

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN-SIGAL
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to requiring certain
state owned and operated parking garages, open parking lots and other
parking facilities to install and maintain charging stations for plug-in
electric vehicles

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would require all New York State owned and operated parking
garages, open parking lots and other parking facilities to install and
maintain a set amount of charging stations for Plug-In Electric Vehi-
cles.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Requires any parking garage, open parking lot and other park-
ing facility owned and/or operated by the State of New York, that offers
between 50 and 200 parking spaces for the purposes of public use, state
employee use and pay-per-usage, is hereby required to install electric
charging stations in at least 10 percent of the total number of parking
spaces offered by such facility

Section 2: Requires any parking garage, open parking lot and other park-
ing facility owned and/or operated by the State of New York, that offers
more than 200 parking spaces for the purposes of public use, state
employee use and pay-per-usage, is hereby required to install electric
charging stations in at least 20 percent of the total number of parking
spaces offered by such facility.

Section 3: Sets forth electrical supply and capacity standards for Elec-
tric Vehicle Supply Equipment in open parking lots and other open air
parking facilities.

Section 4: Sets forth electrical supply and capacity standards for Elec-
tric Vehicle Supply Equipment in parking garages.

Section 5: Provides for the installation of Electric Vehicle Supply
Equipment by the Office of General Services or licensed contracting
agency.

Section 6: Provides for the operation, maintenance and repair of Elec-
tric Vehicle Supply Equipment by the Office of General Services or
licensed contacting agency.

Section 7: Outlines parking restrictions and the installation of appro-
priate signage for spaces designated with Electric Vehicle Supply Equip-
ment.

Section 8: Provides for the enforcement of parking restrictions of spac-
es designated with Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment. a

Section 9: Sets forth that New York State bears all installationi oper-
ating and maintenance costs of Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment.

Section 10: This act shall take effect immediately.
 
JUSTIFICATION:

The number of alternative fuel vehicles on the road in both New York
State and across the country has grown significantly over the past
decade. Specifically, Plug-In Electric Vehicles (those that are powered
by an electric fuel cell and can be recharged) are in increasingly high
demand, and market forecast studies conducted by Navigant Research find
that by 2022 2.3 percent of total vehicle sales in the United States are
expected to be Plug-In Electric Vehicles (PEV's) and that New York State
will sell 144,690 PEV's between 2013 and 2022.

Given the large number of PEV vehicles that currently are and will be on
the road by 2020, it is cur duty as a national leader in renewable ener-
gy to provide the citizens of this state, as well as visitors, with
proper resources for them to recharge their vehicles. This bill will
promote individuals who were previously concerned with charging station
limitations within the state to purchase clean energy vehicles, both
boosting the economy through increases in private and state taxable
revenue on the sales of such PEV's. Lastly, this Legislation will bring
New York State up to par with other energy efficient states such as
California and Texas, who are already installing charging stations in an
effort to promote clean and renewable energy and reduce carbon emis-
sions.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.0370-A of 2021-2022 (Hoylman): Passed Senate

A.0346-A of 2021-2022 (Cahill): Died in Governmental Operations

S.2274 of 2019-2020 (Hoylman): Died in Investigations and Government
Operations

A.0033 of 2019-2020 (Cahill): Died in Government Operations

S.5909 of 2017-2018 (Hoylman): Died in Investigations and Government
Operations

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

BILL NUMBER: S1535A

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN-SIGAL
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to requiring certain
state owned and operated parking facilities to install and maintain
charging stations for plug-in electric vehicles

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would require all New York State owned and operated parking
garages, open parking lots and other parking facilities to install and
maintain a set amount of charging stations for Plug-In Electric Vehi-
cles.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one would add a new section 201-b to the executive law requiring
the installation of electric vehicle charging stations in state owned
and operated parking facilities and would provide a definition of "park-
ing facility" for the purposes of this section.  Further, it would set
forth requirements for the amount of electric vehicle charging stations
that must be installed respective to the number of parking spaces within
the parking facility and would provide that such charging stations must
follow applicable state and local electrical codes. The Office of Gener-
al Services (OGS) would be responsible for the installation and mainte-
nance of electric vehicle supply equipment.

Section two would set forth the effective date.

The number of alternative fuel vehicles on the road in both New York
State and across the country has grown significantly over the past
decade. Specifically, Plug-In Electric Vehicles (those that are powered
by an electric fuel cell and can be recharged) are in increasingly high

expected to be Plug-In Electric Vehicles (PEV's) and that New York State
will sell 144,690 PEV's between 2013 and 2022.

Given the large number of PEV vehicles that currently are and will be on
the road by 2020, it is cur duty as a national leader in renewable ener-
gy to provide the citizens of this state, as well as visitors, with
proper resources for them to recharge their vehicles. This bill will
promote individuals who were previously concerned with charging station
limitations within the state to purchase clean energy vehicles, both
boosting the economy through increases in private and state taxable
revenue on the sales of such PEV's. Lastly, this Legislation will bring
New York State up to par with other energy efficient states such as
California and Texas, who are already installing charging stations in an
effort to promote clean and renewable energy and reduce carbon emis-
sions.

S.2274 of 2019-2020 (Hoylman): Died in Investigations and Government
Operations

S.5909 of 2017-2018 (Hoylman): Died in Investigations and Government
Operations

To be determined.

This act shall take effect immediately.
